_about: Daily nutrient targets for complementary foods of breastfed children, used by the Module 3 optimiser. NEEDS NUTRITIONIST SIGN-OFF before any plan reaches caregivers.
method: Follows de Jager et al. 2018 (northern Ghana, Optifood): FAO/WHO 2004 RNIs, iron at 5% bioavailability, adequacy = at least 70% of RNI. Unlike Optifood, breast milk's contribution is NOT subtracted: percentages report what these foods alone supply against the full daily RNI, so they understate the child's true total intake (breast milk adds vitamin A, calcium and vitamin C; it adds little iron and zinc).

fao_who_2004.title: FAO/WHO Vitamin and mineral requirements in human nutrition, 2nd edition (2004)
fao_who_2004.note: Values read from Table 15 (vitamin C), Table 18 (vitamin A safe intake), Table 40 (iron, 5% bioavailability), Table 56 (zinc, low bioavailability) and Appendix 1 (calcium).

energy_from_complementary_foods.title: WHO/PAHO Guiding principles for complementary feeding of the breastfed child (2003), based on Dewey & Brown 2003
energy_from_complementary_foods.note: 200 / 300 / 550 kcal a day at 6-8 / 9-11 / 12-23 months for average breast-milk intake in developing countries. Quoted consistently in secondary sources (including de Jager et al. 2018's references); the primary document could not be opened during this build. Confirm before use.

de_jager_2018.title: de Jager, Giller & Brouwer 2018, Food and nutrient gaps in rural Northern Ghana, PLOS ONE (PMC6136797)

_notes: Zinc: FAO/WHO low-bioavailability values (unrefined cereal diets). Table 56 gives 8.4 mg at 7-12 months and 8.3 mg at 1-3 years; Appendix 1 swaps the two. Table 56 is used. de Jager et al. used IZiNCG values instead.

Vitamin A: FAO/WHO 'recommended safe intake' in ug RE; WAFCT's RAE column is used as the closest match (RAE counts carotenoids at half the value of RE, so plant-source vitamin A is under- rather than over-credited).
The same RNIs apply to 6-8 and 9-11 months (FAO/WHO 7-12 month band); only the energy budget differs.
